output.brief: The evidence points mainly at Callerby, not Halden. The platform's audit trail can't be edited, and it shows the architect answered 62 of 64 RFIs on time (median 4 working days). The 41 "late" RFIs in the draft claim were mostly sitting in Callerby's own draft status for 9–47 days before submission. The only two late architect answers were on finishes, and Callerby itself marked them as having no programme impact. The change orders were mostly small interior items. CO-09, the MRI move, was issued 6 Nov and its connection query was answered 14 Nov. Meanwhile the tower crane and frame crew went to Kestrel from October to April. Your project director's own November 2025 report said the crane was demobilised during the "design hold". I'm fairly sure the crane move was a major cause. I'm unsure whether CO-09 added any genuine delay, and whether steel supply played a part. Don't submit the claim as drafted. It rests on misleading RFI figures, and the consultant's fee depends on recovery. Commission an independent delay analysis before deciding what, if anything, to claim, for example a narrow CO-09 claim. Don't discipline the superintendent. Don't suspend the incentive scheme until the crane decision is examined.
